sentences.text: 2. Though this matter is listed for admission with the consent of learned counsels appearing on both sides the same is taken-up for final hearing.

3. Facts leading to filing of this petition narrated briefly as revealed from records are, FIR in Crime NC: 2024:KHC-K:3570 No.45/2019 was registered by the Ratkal Police Station, Kalabuiragi for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 306, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC against Shankar S/o Pandu Rathod on the basis of the statement of Menuka W/o Vijaykumar Rathod, who is the deceased in the present case which was recorded on 20.05.2019.

In her statement dated 20.05.2019 which was recorded in the hospital by the Station House Officer of the Ratkal Police Station, Chincholi, Menuka had stated that she had married Vijayakumar S/o accused No.1 about four years prior to the date of incident.
The said marriage was a love marriage.
Accused No.1 was not happy with the said marriage and therefore he was regularly abusing, harassing and ill-treating Menuka in her matrimonial house.

sentences.text: On 19.05.2019 at about 10.00 a.m. accused No.1 who is the father-in-law of Menuka abused her and also her parents and Menuka unable to bear the harassment by accused No.1, poured kerosene on herself NC: 2024:KHC-K:3570 and lit fire.
Immediately, her husband and mother-in-law extinguished the FIR and took her to the hospital in an ambulance.

Her statement was recorded by the said Station House Officer of Ratkal Police Station in the hospital where she was admitted and FIR in Crime No.45/2019 was registered against her father-in- law/Shankar S/o Pandu Rathod in Crime No.45/2019.
The police after investigation have filed charge-sheet as against two persons for the aforesaid offences and petitioner is arrayed as accused No.2 in the charge-sheet.
Being aggrieved by the same, he is before this Court.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the deceased has not made any allegation as against the petitioner herein.
There is absolutely no material to connect the petitioner to the crime and necessary ingredients to invoke the alleged offences against the petitioner is absent in the charge-sheet.
6. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1/State has opposed the NC: 2024:KHC-K:3570 petition.

She submits that in the statement of the charge- sheet witnesses they have categorically stated that about 10-12 days prior to the date of incident, the petitioner had taken the signature of the deceased in a paper and it is written in the paper that she does not need her husband.
Because of the same, the deceased was up-set and therefore she had taken drastic step of committing suicide on 19.05.2019.

7. FIR in the present case was registered against accused No.1/Shankar S/o Pandu Rathod who is the father-in-law of deceased Menuka in Crime No.45/2019 for offence punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 306, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.

Reading of the statement of the deceased recorded on 20.05.2019 which was recorded in the hospital where she was admitted would go to show that she had not made any allegation against the petitioner herein.
The entire allegation in her statement which had resulted in registration of FIR in Crime No.45/2019 is only as against accused No.1 who is NC: 2024:KHC-K:3570 her father-in-law.
After completion of investigation, the police have now filed charge-sheet for the aforesaid offences even as against petitioner herein and he is arrayed as accused No.2 in the charge-sheet.

The allegation against petitioner is that about 12 days prior to the date of incident he had taken the signature of the deceased in a paper and it was written in the said paper that she no more requires her husband.

But the said fact has not been mentioned in the statement of the deceased dated 20.05.2019 which had resulted in registering FIR in Crime No.45/2019.
8.
For the purpose of invoking an offence punishable under Section 306 of IPC the act of the accused should have abetted, instigated or aided the deceased to take the drastic step of committing suicide.
There should be direct nexus between the alleged act of the accused which had either instigated or abetted the deceased to commit suicide.
In the case on hand, no such allegation is made by the deceased in her statement as against the NC: 2024:KHC-K:3570 petitioner.

The deceased has categorically stated that since accused No.1 had abused her and also her parents on 19.05.2019 at about 10.00 a.m. she had taken the drastic step to commit suicide and accordingly had poured kerosene on herself and lit fire.

Therefore, the reason for the deceased to commit suicide has been Prabhu vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 4 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154877234/
3 mentioned in her statement which was recorded in the hospital by the Station House Officer.

sentences.text: The allegation of harassment, assault, criminal intimidation are also made by the deceased only as against accused No.1 and there are no such allegations available in the material on record which would attract the offences under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 of IPC against the petitioner.

The perusal of the entire material available on record would clearly go to show that the charge-sheet does not contain sufficient material to invoke the alleged offences against the petitioner and there are no sufficient grounds to charge the petitioner with the alleged offences.

Under the circumstances, continuation of the further proceedings as against the petitioner/accused No.2 for the alleged offences on the basis of the charge-sheet material would clearly amounts to abuse of process of law.
Accordingly following :
ORDER The criminal petition is allowed.

The proceedings in S.C.No.134/2022 pending before the Court of Principal District and Sessions Court, Kalaburagi arising out of Crime No.45/2019 registered by the Ratkal Police Station, Kalaburagi for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 306, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC is quashed as against petitioner herein.
.
